transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in today? Is there something specific that's been troubling you or that you'd like to talk about?

Yeah… I guess the main thing is I can’t stop thinking about how I look, especially my hairline and my face. I work under these bright restaurant lights, and I feel like they make every angle of my face look… old, kind of strange, like people must be noticing it as soon as they see me.

My coworkers tell me they don’t see what I’m talking about, and they’ll say I look fine, but I don’t know… I can’t really take that in. It’s like I see something different. I keep getting stuck on it, and it’s been really bothering me.
Do you find yourself doing anything repeatedly, like checking mirrors, trying to hide the area, or seeking reassurance, because of how you feel about your appearance?

Yeah, I do. I mean… more than I want to admit, honestly. Before a shift, especially, it becomes this whole routine that I can’t seem to stop. I’ll go into the bathroom and check the mirror over and over, not just once like a normal person fixing their hair, but from different distances and angles, turning my head, looking at the hairline, then my face, then back again.

Sometimes I take pictures on my phone because I don’t trust what I’m seeing in the mirror, but then the pictures are worse because I’ll take one from the side, one under the light, one with my head tilted, and then I’m zooming in and comparing them. I’ll comb my hair forward to try to cover the hairline, then I’ll think it looks obvious or fake, so I redo it again. It can eat up so much time.

And the whole time I’m thinking about how the guests are going to see me when I’m standing at the front, like whether they’ll notice right away or be looking at that part of my face instead of just talking to me. I replay it in my head before I even walk out there. There have been times I’m late getting to the front or I’m so worked up I just stand there trying to calm down before I can go out.
When you look in the mirror or at pictures of yourself, are you focused on something you believe is a flaw or defect in your appearance that others probably don’t even notice?

Yes… that’s exactly it. I know it probably sounds strange, but when I look in the mirror or see a picture, my eyes go right to my hairline and then to the way my face looks, especially under the lights at work. It’s like I’m looking for proof that I look old or odd somehow.

And the thing is, my coworkers will say they don’t see it, or that I look normal, but I can’t really believe them. I keep thinking maybe they’re just being nice, or they don’t want to embarrass me. To me it feels obvious, like the restaurant lights make every line and angle on my face stand out, and my hairline looks like the first thing people would notice. I get stuck on it even when other people say there’s nothing there.

latest_inference.note: The patient's symptoms are highly consistent with Body Dysmorphic Disorder (BDD), which is coded as F45.22. The symptoms include preoccupation with perceived defects in appearance, repetitive behaviors (e.g., mirror checking, photographing, camouflaging), and significant distress or impairment in functioning. The presentation rules out Generalized Anxiety Disorder (F41.1) and Major Depressive Disorder (F32.9) as primary diagnoses, as the anxiety and potential depressive symptoms appear to be secondary to the body image concerns.
